newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan sees end to wheat shortages.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan sees end to wheat shortages.

text.p: Pakistan, facing an acute shortage of wheat, expects to receive 472,500 tonnes of wheat by the middle of May, and plans no more imports for now, a senior government official said on Thursday.
Food and Agriculture Ministry secretary Mahboob Ahmad told Reuters that two ships, each carrying 47,250 tonnes of wheat, would arrive at Karachi port on April 13 and 15.
Six more ships carrying the same quantity each will arrive between April 20 and 30 and the last two ships in May, he added.

The wheat shortage has sparked riots in the North West Frontier Province and southwestern province of Baluchistan over the past week, but Ahmed said the crisis would end by next week when more stocks of imported and domestic wheat would reach the markets.

He said the government had no plans to import more wheat for the present because the new domestic crop would be available in the market by May and the shipments of imported wheat would be enough to meet the demand.
"Pakistan has no plan to import more wheat because it takes at least 40 days to arrive and by that time our local produce will also be in the market," he said.
He said new-crop wheat had started arriving in the southern province of Sindh and was expected to arrive in the first week of May in the main growing central province of Punjab.
"The farmers had slightly delayed harvesting to get better prices, which the government announced on April 3," Ahmad said.
Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif raised the government's support price for wheat to 240 rupees ($5.96) per 40 kg from 185 rupees ($4.50) in an agriculture package announced last week.
Ahmed said the new crop was likely to be "more or less" the same as 1995/96 (July-June) output of 17.57 million tonnes.
He said the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) had loaned 10,000 tonnes of wheat to the government from its stocks in Quetta and Peshawar to meet shortages.
A WFP statement said on Thursday it had released the wheat to Pakistan from its stocks for Afghanistan but that would not affect the humanitarian assistance in the war-torn country.
The WFP said it would return an additional 20,280 tonnes of wheat to Pakistan that it had earlier borrowed from Islamabad, when its new stocks arrived on April 20.
Pakistan, which blames the shortages on smuggling to neighbouring countries, particularly to Afghanistan, hoarding and late arrival of imports, closed its borders last month.
